criteria.justification: The response explicitly separates the reviewer’s “goal” of simplicity and one unified view from the “proposed mechanism” of overwriting, stating that the research supports only the former.

It identifies the existing field as “load-bearing for millions of existing records and external integrations” and explains that overwriting would silently make the field answer a different question depending on read time, creating an effectively untraceable breaking change.
The response rejects two linked records because they could produce “duplicate alerts for one incident” and would push correlation burdens onto consumers or require compensating alert-layer logic.
It clearly selects Option Three: one event with one lifecycle, the original field retaining its current semantics, and an additive second field holding the refined estimate.

The response validates the reviewer’s customer-simplicity objective and argues that Option Three achieves it without the breaking-change risk; it also proposes satisfying any one-number UI preference at the presentation layer.
